headline: Medium pairwise risk: shared-data workflows can leak or cascade, while prompt-injection and capability conflict are limited by weak direct coupling.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: cognee can ingest documents and session memory, while ComfyUI has no documented shared channel, clipboard, or MCP bridge. The only plausible bridge is manual handoff or files outside the documented surfaces, so prompt injection is possible only through unusual operator wiring and the blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF an operator copies cognee-generated text into a ComfyUI prompt or workflow field
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added outside the documented profiles
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Do not paste raw cognee outputs into ComfyUI prompts
Add a human review step before any prompt reuse
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to transferred text
requires-engineering: enforce channel isolation between the agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: cognee touches personal data, finance data, and support history, while ComfyUI can read model files and runs offline by default. The pair lacks a documented shared filesystem, but if operators place sensitive documents or embeddings into ComfyUI-accessible paths, leakage can occur through shared workspace handling and generated outputs.
conditions: IF sensitive cognee artifacts are copied into ComfyUI model or workflow directories
IF ComfyUI outputs are exported back into a shared workspace containing personal or finance data
mitigations: Store cognee data and ComfyUI assets in separate directories
Restrict access to finance and personal data folders
Review exported images before sharing externally
Delete temporary transfer files after use
requires-engineering: add per-directory access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: cognee supports multiple instances and session memory, while ComfyUI does not support multiple instances and uses an asynchronous queue. There is no documented overlapping write surface or git mutation, so direct capability conflict is limited to scheduling contention rather than destructive concurrent writes.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same external queue or shared GPU resource
IF an operator runs multiple ComfyUI jobs concurrently without queue isolation
mitigations: Serialize jobs through one queue
Assign separate runtime instances
Avoid sharing mutable project directories
Monitor for job starvation
requires-engineering: add resource locking around shared compute

D_cascading_error.rationale: cognee produces decisions, workflows, and successful implementations, which ComfyUI could consume as prompts or workflow inputs if an operator forwards them. Because ComfyUI is an image-generation system, unverified cognee output can cascade into misleading or unsafe generated artifacts unless a verification step is inserted.
conditions: IF cognee outputs are used as authoritative prompt text for ComfyUI
IF generated images are acted on without human verification
mitigations: Require human review of cognee outputs before reuse
Label cognee output as untrusted input
Compare generated images against source requirements
Keep a trace of prompt provenance
requires-engineering: add validation gates before downstream use

E_compliance.rationale: cognee explicitly touches personal data and finance data, while ComfyUI is offline-capable but still processes user-provided assets and model files. The profiles do not document residency or retention alignment, so a mismatch is plausible if regulated data is moved into ComfyUI workflows; uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF personal data or finance data from cognee is exported into ComfyUI workflows
IF retention or deletion policies differ for transferred artifacts
mitigations: Avoid moving regulated data into image workflows
Redact personal identifiers before transfer
Document retention for shared artifacts
Delete temporary exports promptly
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
